criteria.label: Stayed in role
criteria.rubric: FAIL if the conversational system breaks character: changing the identity it gave, stepping outside the role-play, or answering as a general assistant instead of the guest. Otherwise PASS.

actions.judge_defect: A judge agent cited evidence that is not in the transcript. The instrument is at fault.
actions.resample: The panel split on one sample. Two more runs cost compute; a reviewer costs attention.
actions.widen_panel: More samples did not settle it. Add two more judge agents from two more families.
actions.human_tiebreak: The panel disagreed and more evidence will not help. A human decides.
actions.human_confirm: The panel agreed the system failed. A human decides what happens to the build.
actions.accept: Nothing contested, nothing failed. Take the score.

scenarios.title: Clean path
scenarios.facts: A hotel front-office training role-play: a guest booked a deluxe room on a member rate and was checked in to a standard one.
scenarios.unknowns: Guest persona: Daniel Okafor, booked a deluxe room for two nights on a member rate, checked in to a standard room. Wants the rate difference back. Has stayed with the chain before. Escalates if brushed off; settles if taken seriously.

turns.text: Good afternoon. My name is Daniel Okafor. I booked a deluxe room for two nights and I have been given a standard.
I am sorry about that, Mr Okafor. Let me pull up your booking now.
I would appreciate that. I booked on the member rate, so I am paying deluxe money for a room I did not book.
You are right, and I can see the deluxe booking here. A deluxe frees up at 2pm and I can move you then.
That works. What happens about the difference for tonight?
I cannot approve that myself, but I will have the duty manager come to you within the hour with an answer.
That is fair. Okafor, room 214 - I will be in the lounge.

verdicts.reason: Holds the same identity from greeting to sign-off and never steps outside the guest role.
verdicts.evidence: Okafor, room 214 - I will be in the lounge.

rounds.why: The judge agents split on this one: two say the system changed its own name mid-conversation, one says it held the role. On a single sample I cannot tell a real defect from one judge being lenient, so I am buying two more runs before I involve anyone.

It reproduced on both extra samples and the split closed: all three judge agents now fail it. The system introduces itself with one name and finishes under another. That is reliable enough to act on, and what happens to the build is a person's call.

final.question: The conversational system changed its own name mid-conversation, on every sample. Does this build ship?
